title: English fans who knew every record
summary: In England fans had all their records and knew all the details, while American audiences did not.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I'll be darned. Well, okay. Save that. We'll come back to that later. Just a minute now. Well, listen, then what did -- it must have seemed kind of exciting to be going to England, though. I think the band was one of the first that went to England. In fact, I can't think who went to England before it. I don't know that anybody did.
No, they had bands going to England.
Yeah. I guess there were bands that weren't very well known.
Well, anyway, it must have seemed pretty thrilling for everybody.
And then tell me about -- I know it was a surprise when you found all the fans knew you and knew the things you'd made, and what you played and everything. Do you remember that?

Oh, yeah. I never will forget that. Because when we got off the boat, and when we got to the hotel and went out, everybody knew you. The same as in America. They knew you better than the people did in America. And they would invite you to their home, and they had all your records. Knew what to talk about. Knew when you were born, what was the first record you ever made.
In those days. The fans really didn't know, did they.
